changelog: **External Correction — priority control**: three-way switch governing how external correction and user mouse input share control. *User Priority* (correction smoothly fades out while the hand is moving), *Corrector Priority* (full correction, previous behaviour), *Weighted* (constant blend factor 0–1 via slider).

**External Correction — object-switch suppression**: prediction-based gating rejects frames that fall outside a configurable radius around the predicted target position (velocity-extrapolated), so alternating detections of multiple objects no longer cause the correction to jump. A confirmed object switch requires N consecutive consistent frames (configurable 1–10) and then performs a hard reset onto the new target.
**External Correction — light prediction**: optional extrapolation of the target by `velocity × frame age` (0–100 % weight) to compensate measurement latency. Uses the new frame-age field.

**External Correction — target-switch reset & deadband**: innovation above a threshold resets the EMA onto the new target instead of slewing through (active when gate is off); a deadband suppresses micro-jitter output near the target.

**External Correction — additive MIM spline feed-forward**: new "Add. MIM/CIM Splines" toggle (default OFF) applies the MIM velocity-spline correction on top of the external correction, scaled by a 0–1 weight slider.

**External Correction — slew-rate limiter**: optional "Max Step" limit (0–100 px, 0 = off) caps the correction magnitude per report while preserving direction (X/Y scaled uniformly), so a brief target outlier can no longer cause a single-report lurch — the correction approaches the target at a controlled maximum speed. Applies to Classic/Adaptive modes.

**External Correction — v2 frame format**: parser accepts the new 9-byte `0xFE` frames carrying a 16-bit frame-age field alongside the legacy 7-byte `0xFF` format. Stale frames (age > sample window) are discarded; the GUI shows the last frame age next to the signal lamp.
**AIM — key capture in Python GUI**: button map entries are set by clicking "Set" and pressing the desired key or mouse button (including side buttons) instead of typing hex codes; "×" clears a slot.

**AIM profile persistence**: modifier key codes (LCtrl, LShift, … 0xE0–0xE7) are now accepted by profile validation and `set_aim_mapping`. Previously the default map failed its own validation, so the AIM profile silently reverted to defaults on every reboot and GUI writes containing modifiers were discarded.
**AIM key output**: mapped keyboard keys are now translated from HID usage IDs to Teensyduino key codes before sending — previously e.g. a mapped Space key typed a comma.

**EEPROM profile corruption**: `ExtCorrProfile` (@416) and `CounterStrafeProfile` (@434) overlapped by 22 bytes — saving either profile invalidated the other's CRC, causing settings to randomly reset. Counter-Strafe profile relocated to address 480.
**MKCOMBO mode**: survives the mode-switch reboot; `loadActiveMode()` previously rejected the pending MKCOMBO token and fell back to auto-detection.
